task:
When EO finishes building a repository index it does not trust the exit code — it re-reads the index and confirms one is there. A sync already reports how many files it changed, and that number reaches the row EO keeps for the index. A first build reports no such number, so a freshly built index has a blank where a sync leaves a count.

Give a successful first build the same treatment: report how many files were indexed, carry it to the same place the sync's count goes, and cover it with tests.

Take the smaller reading of anything ambiguous and note it in your handoff rather than asking.

args.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
import re
p="apps/desktop/src/main/repositoryIntelligence/port.ts"
s=open(p).read()
old = """      /**
       * How many files the implementation reported updating.
       *
       * Meaningful for an update of an existing index and absent for a
       * build from nothing, where "changed" would mean "all of them" and
       * would say nothing anyone asked. Reported by the implementation
       * rather than computed by the caller: a checkout carries
       * uncommitted work that a commit-to-commit diff would miss, and
       * the thing that just walked the tree already knows the answer.
       */
      changedFileCount?: number;"""
new = """      /**
       * How many files the index now accounts for as a result of this
       * work: what an update reported changing, or what a build from
       * nothing put in the index.
       *
       * Both, and not only the update, because a build that answered
       * nothing left a row with a blank where every other successful
       * build leaves a number — and a blank reads as "never measured"
       * rather than as "measured, and the answer was every file". The
       * two readings want opposite things from whoever is looking at
       * the row.
       *
       * Reported by the implementation rather than computed by the
       * caller, and for the same reason in both cases: a checkout
       * carries uncommitted work that a commit-to-commit diff would
       * miss, and the thing that just walked the tree already knows the
       * answer.
       *
       * Still optional. Not every implementation of this port has to
       * count anything, and a caller that only wants to know whether
       * the index is usable must not have to care.
       */
      changedFileCount?: number;"""
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,"w").write(s)
PY
echo ok

args.old_string:
* So `problem` carries the account of the verification for whoever
   * asked for a build, `getStatus` projects it away for whoever asked
   * for a probe, and the type makes the pairing impossible to get wrong:
   * there is no way to spell "not present, and no reason why".
   */
  type Verification = { present: true; probe: RepositoryIndexProbe } | { present: false; probe: RepositoryIndexProbe; problem: string };
args.new_string:
* So `problem` carries the account of the verification for whoever
   * asked for a build, `getStatus` projects it away for whoever asked
   * for a probe, and the type makes the pairing impossible to get wrong:
   * there is no way to spell "not present, and no reason why".
   *
   * `files` is the other half of the same asymmetry. A verification that
   * found an index has read the tool's own description of it, and that
   * description carries a number a build wants to report; a verification
   * that found nothing has no number to carry, and the type says so
   * rather than offering a zero that would read as an empty index.
   */
  type Verification =
    | { present: true; probe: RepositoryIndexProbe; files: number }
    | { present: false; probe: RepositoryIndexProbe; problem: string };
